clue.text: A victory with two characters finally released from court

indicators.note: the last two letters of the word are let go, dropped from its end

parts.note: a victory is a triumph

explanation.surface: A win sees two people at last let out of a law court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two characters finally released' removes PH, the last two letters of TRIUMPH, leaving TRIUM. The 'court' is not a law court but an open inner courtyard.
explanation.definitionFit: An open central hall or courtyard of a house or building, as in Roman architecture.

clue.text: What's used for painting sacred building, with pounds spent on artist

indicators.note: the pounds are used up, so that letter disappears from the building

parts.note: a temple is a sacred building
L is the abbreviation for pounds (libra)
RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword artist

explanation.surface: A list of what goes into a church painting, money spent on the artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spent' takes L out of TEMPLE, leaving TEMPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Egg-based paint medium used by painters, especially before oils became common.

clue.text: Spring edition

definitions.meaning: to spring or flow out, as a stream ... from the ground
a particular printing of a magazine

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: to flow out of a source, and one numbered release of a periodical.

clue.text: Country club joined by academic, international ace

parts.note: a mace is a heavy club
a don is a university teacher
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

explanation.surface: A country club takes on an academic who is also an international star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country club' reads as one phrase, but splits into the definition and MACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A Balkan nation, now officially North Macedonia, and earlier an ancient kingdom.

clue.text: Gong given to performer who tried to bring reform?

parts.note: CH, Companion of Honour, is a British honour or gong
an artist is a performer

explanation.surface: A medal handed to an entertainer who campaigned for change.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'gong' is British slang for a medal or honour; CH is the Companion of Honour. The Chartists were a 19th-century British movement demanding voting reform.
explanation.definitionFit: Member of the 1830s-40s working-class movement campaigning for the People's Charter of electoral reforms.

clue.text: Criminal pair one found in sect

indicators.note: these two pieces are located within the sect's word, placed inside it

parts.note: a cult is a sect
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A lawbreaking couple turn up inside a religious cult.
explanation.definitionFit: The person guilty of an offence, the wrongdoer.

clue.text: Like layer that's very pale

parts.note: as means like
a hen lays eggs, so is a layer

explanation.surface: Describing a coat of paint that is extremely light in colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'layer' suggests a coat or stratum; here it is something that lays eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey and drained of colour, like ashes.

clue.text: Half of them on trail collapsing in demanding race

indicators.note: falling apart, so the letters are reassembled in a new order
the first half of the word, two of its four letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Half the competitors fall apart on the course during a tough race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half of them' gives TH; with ON TRAIL these letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An endurance contest of swimming, cycling and running back to back.

clue.text: Dubious American Pastor in dissenting body

indicators.note: the two pieces sit inside the word for the dissenting body

parts.note: a sect is a group breaking away from a main church

explanation.surface: An American minister within a breakaway church seems questionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Questionable or not to be trusted, as a suspect claim.

clue.text: Party activity shows such racialism unfortunately

indicators.note: an unhappy outcome signals the letters going wrong, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A party shows a regrettable prejudice.
explanation.walkthrough: SUCH RACIALISM rearranged gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's party game where players scramble for one fewer seat than there are of them.

clue.text: Sort of footballer put off when goal goes in?

indicators.note: the goal's word is placed inside the put-off word

parts.note: to defer is to put off
an end is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: A player postponed when a goal is scored.
explanation.walkthrough: The football surface makes 'goal' look literal; here it is END, an aim.
explanation.definitionFit: A player whose role is to stop the opposition scoring, a back.

clue.text: Name given to complete crackpot

parts.note: utter means complete, total

explanation.surface: Calling someone a total eccentric.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British term for a crazy or eccentric person.

clue.text: The first character to preach (the result of a burning desire?)

definitions.text: The first character to preach (the result of a burning desire?)

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the following word is taken

parts.words: the result of a burning desire
parts.note: arson is what a desire to burn things leads to

explanation.surface: A preacher's opening line, perhaps fired by passionate longing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a clergyman, one whose role is to preach, with the burning desire hinting at hellfire sermons.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish clergyman, whose job is to deliver sermons.

clue.text: One extending a provision for injured players

definitions.meaning: a litter for carrying hurt players off the field

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a device that stretches things, and a frame for carrying the injured.

clue.text: Model secretary holding everyone else up?

parts.note: a temp is a temporary secretary
someone who is late keeps everyone else waiting

explanation.surface: A model secretary who delays the whole office?
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern or guide to be copied, a model.

clue.text: Savage acts bringing terrible scare to large number

parts.note: a mass is a large number

indicators.note: the word is in a terrible state, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Brutal deeds bring dreadful fear to crowds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges the letters of 'scare'; 'bringing ... to' joins the large number to them, the large number coming first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaughters of many people, brutal killings.

clue.text: In the course of fights thrash Greeks

indicators.note: the thrash word happens during, so inside, the fights word

parts.note: spars means fights, as in boxing practice
to tan someone's hide is to thrash them

explanation.surface: During battles, Greeks are given a beating.
explanation.definitionFit: Citizens of Sparta, an ancient Greek city-state.

clue.text: Soldier only briefly gets overhead protection

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: solo means only, alone

explanation.surface: A soldier, if only for a moment, gets cover from above.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunshade held over the head.

clue.text: Block a series of steps with two pianos? That looks dotty!

indicators.note: to block is to plug, so the pianos fill the middle of the steps

parts.note: a stile is a set of steps over a fence
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft, so two give PP

explanation.surface: Blocking a staircase with two pianos seems crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: A stile is a set of steps for climbing over a fence or wall. 'dotty' means crazy on the surface but literally dotted here.
explanation.definitionFit: A technique of painting or engraving with small dots, giving a dotted look.

clue.text: Wood that gets walked in a lot in summer?

definitions.meaning: a fragrant timber, as in sandalwood

definitions.text: that gets walked in a lot in summer?
definitions.meaning: a light open shoe for warm weather

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: the scented tree's timber, and an open summer shoe.

clue.text: Drunk sat in a part of the wine cellar — to kick his habit?

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go inside the other pieces

parts.note: a bin is a rack for bottles in a wine cellar

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A drunk sitting among the wine racks, maybe trying to quit drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' scrambles the letters of 'sat'. A bin is a numbered rack in a wine cellar; 'in' sets the scramble inside it, after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain from something, especially from alcohol, giving up a habit.

clue.text: Idiot journalist blabbered

parts.note: a prat is British slang for an idiot
ED, editor, is the crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A foolish reporter talked too much.
explanation.definitionFit: Talked at length foolishly, chattered.

clue.text: A number practise a form of Buddhism

parts.note: to do is to practise or perform
Zen is a school of Buddhism

explanation.surface: Several people practise a type of Buddhism.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve, a specific quantity.

clue.text: How brief announcement may be given on screen suddenly

definitions.text: How brief announcement may be given on screen
definitions.meaning: a newsflash appears on screen as a brief bulletin

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: shown as a newsflash, and occurring instantaneously.

clue.text: Ship is tarry, not good

indicators.note: the good letter is excluded, taken away

parts.note: to linger is to tarry

explanation.surface: A ship is covered in tar, and not in good shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tarry' looks like an adjective, covered in tar; it is the verb, to linger.
explanation.definitionFit: A large passenger ship on a regular route.

clue.text: One Irish chap jigging around — last character in that unfortunate mental state

indicators.note: the last character goes inside the rearranged letters
dancing a jig, so the letters move around into a new order

parts.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A dancing Irishman, completely mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jigging around' scrambles the three words as one pool, and 'in' slips the alphabet's last letter into the result; 'that' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A serious psychiatric disorder affecting perception and thought.

clue.text: Name of nurse in Italian city

definitions.meaning: ... Nightingale, the famous Crimean War nurse

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: the first name of Nightingale, and the city she was named after.

clue.text: Violent street with wicked leader bumped off

indicators.note: the first letter is killed off, removed

parts.note: wrong means wicked

explanation.surface: A rough street where the gang boss has been murdered.
explanation.definitionFit: Forceful or intense, as in a strong wind or a strong reaction.
